data.summary: In two weeks the student will front‑load the weak Unit 6 material, then use the second week for a rapid mixed review of all units and timed practice. Each week stays within the 10‑hour limit and includes concrete practice tasks.

weeks.focus: Build mastery of Integration and Accumulation (Unit 6) while refreshing core differentiation concepts.
tasks: Watch a tutorial on Riemann sums and complete 5 practice problems on approximating areas, checking work with the answer key.
Do 8 free‑response questions on the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, then grade them using the AP scoring guidelines.
Complete a worksheet on basic derivative rules (power rule, chain rule) with 10 problems, marking any errors.
Solve 4 applied rate‑of‑change problems (position, velocity, acceleration) and compare solutions to provided solutions.

weeks.focus: Mixed review of all units and timed AP‑style practice.
tasks: Take a 45‑minute timed practice test covering limits, derivatives, and integration; review each answer using the scoring guide.
Do 6 free‑response questions on related rates and differential equations, then self‑grade.
Complete a mixed‑topic worksheet: 2 limit estimation problems, 2 Mean Value Theorem questions, 2 area‑between‑curves integrals.
Review errors from the timed test, writing a one‑sentence explanation for each mistake.

data.final_week_advice: After the two‑week sprint, keep a daily 30‑minute habit of timed free‑response drills and review any lingering weak spots, especially integration techniques.
